title: Push a wooden toy train round a bend by its last wagon, keeping all four vehicles coupled and in the grooves
instruction: Push the toy train counter-clockwise round the track only by the back face of its last wagon, without gripping it or touching the other vehicles, until the engine passes the red finish mark, keeping all four vehicles coupled and every wheel in its groove, then take your hand away.
context: Pushing a wooden toy train round its track is everyday play for children and the adults who play with them. The train is an engine and three wagons held together only by small magnets, and its wheels run in two grooves 3 mm deep. Pushed from behind, the train goes where the grooves steer it, but only if the hand keeps pushing along the track, square to the back of the last wagon, and turns with the bend: a push that cuts across the curve slides off the wagon or drags its end sideways, and a wheel that climbs out of its groove derails the train. A light, steady push is enough, about 0.1 N for this 205 g train. Here the whole train, 33 cm long, is pushed about 30 cm round a tight curve (21.6 cm radius), so every vehicle goes round the bend, and the hand must follow a curved path while it pushes.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. Angles are counter-clockwise from +x about the circle's centre. 1) Track: eight BRIO 33342 large curved tracks (two packs of 4; beech; 170 long each, maker figure) joined into a circle centred at (360, -330), centre-line radius 216 (estimate from the 170 mm length over 45 degrees), 40 wide, 12 thick, with two grooves 6 wide and 3 deep whose centres are 26 apart (estimates); the joints sit at 0, 45, 90 ... degrees and every joint is taped to the table with masking tape. 2) Train: a BRIO 33982 Three-Wagon Cargo Train (beech and plastic; 333 long, 34 wide, 50 high coupled, maker figures; about 205 g, estimate): the wooden cargo engine in front, then the load wagon with the orange container, the load wagon with the light green container and, last, the yellow cargo wagon with sliding doors and its silver motor load inside. The engine leads, facing counter-clockwise; each wagon stands the way round in which its front magnet pulls on the rear magnet of the vehicle ahead (BRIO magnets attract only one way round: turn a wagon end for end if the two push apart). A small pencil tick on the engine's outer side marks its middle, half way between its axles. Coupled and with every wheel in the grooves, it stands with the middles of the vehicles (between their axles) at 183.7 degrees (146, -344), 161.8 (156, -263), 139.9 (196, -192) and 118.0 degrees (259, -140), 215 from the centre. 3) Paper marks just outside the track: the engine's start (183.7 degrees), 10 cm on (210.4), half way (218.7) and the red finish (253.7), 26 cm of track past the start. Both arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Judged from the trial video and a look at the end. Coupled: each pair of neighbouring vehicles has its coupling magnets touching. In the grooves: every wheel down in its groove (none on a rail top or off the track) and every vehicle upright. Lifted: at any time a vehicle was in the air, its lowest point more than 1 cm above the rail tops (picked up or carried). Pushing rule: the train may be moved only by pushing on the back face of the last wagon; gripping any vehicle, or touching the engine, the load wagons or the last wagon anywhere but its back face (with that face's top edge, up to 8 mm onto the roof), breaks it; touches are judged on the wrist-camera views of the trial video. Hands clear: both grippers at least 3 cm from every vehicle at the end. The engine's progress is where its middle (half way between its axles, marked by a small pencil tick on its outer side) stands against the paper marks. Score the first that applies. 0: a vehicle was lifted, or the pushing rule broken, at any time. 1.0: the engine's middle at or past the red finish mark, the train coupled, every wheel in its groove and hands clear. 0.75: past the finish, coupled and every vehicle still on the track, but a wheel out of its groove or a hand still touching. 0.5: the engine's wheels in their grooves and either past the finish with a coupling open, or the train coupled and past the half-way mark. 0.25: the engine's wheels in their grooves at or past the 10 cm mark. 0: anything else (doing nothing scores 0).
reset_notes: About 30 seconds; no consumables beyond a few strips of masking tape. Lift the train off the track, couple it in order (engine, orange-container wagon, green-container wagon, cargo wagon), engine facing counter-clockwise and each wagon the way round in which it pulls onto the vehicle ahead (the magnets attract only one way round; turn a wagon end for end if the two push apart), check that the containers sit on their pins and the motor load is inside the cargo wagon with its doors shut, and set the train down with every wheel in the grooves and the engine's middle at the start mark. Check that the tape still holds every track joint and that no piece has moved (re-tape a loose one). Return both arms to their ready pose. Kit: one BRIO 33982 ($34.99) and two packs of BRIO 33342 ($14.99 each), masking tape and paper marks; under $70.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Each vehicle is one body; its wheels do not turn but slide in the grooves on a low friction (0.04, estimate) that stands for rolling, held sideways only by the groove walls (exact track meshes). The magnetic couplings are forces between points (1.0 N pull-off, estimate; the real ones attract only one way round). Containers and motor load are part of their wagons, as on their pins. Groove, wheel and vehicle sizes and masses are estimates.
